answer: Bind each action to serial work. Every attestation an identity submits must carry a small proof chained to its own secret and its own previous proof — a beacon pulse that must be produced one beat at a time, in order, by that identity alone. A farm’s thousand wallets can run in parallel only if each pays the serial cost in full; buying more machines does not make one wallet write faster. The ledger’s atlas of proofs makes repetition visible, and honest work keeps the rhythm of a quill: deliberate, sequential, and hard to forge by assembly line.
